alternative_architecture.description: Replace the subsystem roadmap with a thin gameplay-delivery lane. State consists of: the human-approved GDD/decision records, small task contracts, integrated main, one append-only attempt/receipt per delivery, and explicit human approvals. Planning is human-prioritized and just-in-time; a single coding worker plans and implements one bounded slice in an isolated worktree. Validation combines scope/diff checks, the existing clean Unity runner, task-specific Edit/Play Mode tests, one fresh semantic review, and a human game-feel/visual gate. Failures return one feedback bundle through at most two repairs. Recovery uses the worktree, checkpoint commits, and a small attempt manifest. After human merge, a receipt binds the integrated commit, relevant canon excerpts, contract revision, test XML, and approval. Readiness derives from merged receipts. GDD edits trigger scoped diff review of referenced sections, not global reconciliation or global invalidation.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It covers state, planning, execution, validation, recovery, and Unity integration while reusing the mechanisms that addressed observed failures. It removes multiple speculative authority and orchestration layers, creates player-visible evidence quickly, and treats design evolution as routine synchronization rather than repeated bootstrap verification.

result.architecture_summary: The architectural kernel is sound: durable state, bounded workers, deterministic checks, Git isolation, Unity/runtime evidence, human authority, and bounded repair are appropriate. The current composition is partially unsound and substantially overbuilt. It has accumulated planning, reconciliation, evidence, provider, and audit machinery without an executable gameplay-delivery path. Worse, its claimed authorities already disagree: canon and task resources name a deleted scene, current code uses the replacement, structural validation still passes, and primary status documents disagree about readiness and implementation stage.
result.biggest_uncertainty: Actual wall-clock leverage remains unmeasured. No real gameplay task has traversed planning, model implementation, Unity validation, repair, merge, and derived completion using the production architecture; the only production conformance record is a retrospective camera baseline.
do_not_build_yet: Continuous supervisor or automatic backlog replenishment.
Parallel workers, claims/leases, resource scheduling, merge queues, or automatic merge.
GitHub Issues/Projects synchronization beyond optional manual links.
Progressive Decomposer and Artifact Authority platform until a real task is blocked by missing design; the initial graph has zero artifact tasks.
More reconciliation verification/refinement machinery for routine changes.
Provider fallback, provider-comparison automation, or additional provider abstractions.
Roslyn/general-purpose project scanning or incremental caches before targeted shell/repository inspection proves insufficient.
Additional immutable evidence layers beyond one concise delivery receipt and underlying test artifacts.

evidence.observation: The frozen commit validates 37 structurally well-formed contracts, but readiness is explicitly unavailable and every autonomous dispatch is denied.

The canonical GDD says the nested DoorPrototype scene is authoritative and the top-level scene is a stub, but that nested scene was deleted and the production builder now saves the populated authoritative scene at Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity.
The production builder directly establishes the new authoritative scene path.

Thirteen task resource claims, PROJECT_REQUIREMENTS, and RESOURCE_GROUPS still lock the deleted scene path. The build-registration task explicitly rejects the scene that is now authoritative. Nevertheless, taskcontrol validate reports PASS.
NSC-037's current contract describes Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity as a non-canonical stub, contradicting the integrated tree.

Conformance binds every delivery to the hash of the entire GDD. Any unrelated GDD edit makes all evidenced tasks stale, while a hash match cannot detect that the GDD itself contains obsolete repository claims.

Conformance evaluates the current HEAD and ancestry but does not verify an integration ref such as main. At the frozen commit, HEAD is provider-adapters while main is at a2b7a78, so 'integrated' cannot be derived from the implemented check alone.

START_HERE claims taskcontrol ready works and identifies seven executable tasks; CURRENT_STATE and the implementation say readiness is unavailable. CURRENT_STATE also says Codex migration is implemented near its beginning but later calls Codex unimplemented and migration the next goal.

Since the Assignment 6 camera commit, 126 commits touched Pipeline/Docs/Tasks but only two touched Assets, both scene/test hardening rather than a new gameplay feature. The diff adds about 115,877 lines to Pipeline/Docs/Tasks.

Current production machinery is about 9,466 Python lines across TaskGraph, AgentRuntime, TaskExecution, and GDDRAG; Reconciliation adds about 15,195 lines, before generated outputs. Task contracts add about 3,283 lines for a prototype with roughly 11 gameplay scripts.
The actual movement implementation still polls Keyboard.current for WASD and has none of the mouse movement, shared pointer projection, restriction, reset, or suspension behavior in NSC-003.

The scene builder still displays 'Hold E to Open', while current canon requires click-to-approach and automatic opening on arrival. This shows substantial gameplay drift remains despite extensive planning machinery.

Assignment 6 records two cases where static evaluation passed an unusable camera and one case where a refiner claimed success without changing Assets. Human Unity testing and a no-progress guard caught them.
The production RAG is current and integrity-checked, but explicitly does not implement task context, scanning, decomposition, artifact authority, supervision, GER integration, or gameplay work.
AgentRuntime currently cannot grant repository writing or approved command execution, so TaskExecution cannot implement or validate gameplay even if a task is manually selected.
Only NSC-023 has committed production conformance evidence; NSC-003 reports not_delivered and no real production revalidation record exists.

gdd_iteration_concerns: The GDD mixes durable game design with volatile repository facts such as canonical scene paths. Those facts changed without the GDD changing, creating two alleged authorities that now contradict each other.

Whole-GDD hashing is safe but too blunt: an unrelated balance, prose, or distant-room edit invalidates every completed task, while an unchanged hash provides no semantic guarantee that repository facts embedded in canon remain true.
Task contracts copy large requirement passages from the GDD. This creates another synchronization surface instead of stable references to governing sections or requirement identities.

For planned work, a relevant GDD change should revise or supersede the task. For active work, it should pause the attempt and require a scoped rebase decision. For delivered work, it should create focused revalidation/remediation only when governing requirements or implementation surfaces changed.

Routine GDD changes need a reviewed impact diff over referenced headings/excerpts. Full reconciliation should be reserved for broad redesign, an exhausted backlog, milestone audits, or suspected systemic drift.

The existing architecture documents acknowledge that scoped impact analysis is eventual, but moving-target synchronization is a current need: the repository already demonstrates canon/task/scene drift.
human_intervention_points: Choose the next player-valued priority; the graph cannot infer product priority.
Resolve NSC-003 input ownership, UI/door/spell click arbitration, click-versus-hold semantics, cancellation, arrival behavior, pathing expectations, and movement-restriction ownership.
Approve GDD changes and classify ambiguous downstream impact.
Judge movement feel, camera framing, readability, visuals, animation, audio, and interaction quality in Play Mode.
Handle Unity serialization/editor work where safe deterministic builders or tests cannot establish the intended result.
Approve architecture-changing prerequisites, shared-resource changes, scope expansion, and generated design/content.
Review and merge early delivery attempts; automatic merge is not justified.
Provide or maintain the Unity host/toolchain and inspect failures that batch execution cannot resolve.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Claims, leases, resource scheduling, and conservative parallelism protect against future multi-worker conflicts; no production multi-worker delivery exists.
GitHub dashboard mirroring, Draft-PR lifecycle automation, merge queues, and continuous scheduling solve future operational scale rather than a present delivery bottleneck.
Artifact Authority, artifact promotion, and artifact GER protect against generated-design misuse, but the initial graph has zero artifact tasks and no observed blocking artifact flow.
Provider fallback and cross-provider equivalence policies solve future availability/portability concerns, not Unity gameplay throughput.
The breadth of immutable provider artifacts, schema attack hardening, historical-directory protection, and anti-tamper evidence checks exceeds failures observed in this trusted single-user project.

A full multi-model reconciliation verification/refinement crew was defensible for the one-time bootstrap, but repeated use for ordinary GDD evolution would address hypothetical semantic corruption at disproportionate cost.
General project scanners, Roslyn analysis, incremental caches, and automatic causal impact models remain speculative until direct repository inspection becomes a measured bottleneck.
missing_components: A write-capable gameplay worker boundary; current providers are read/search only.
A minimal one-task coordinator that creates/resumes an isolated worktree and records checkpoints.
A truthful readiness rule deriving dependency satisfaction from integrated delivery receipts.
A host-side Unity compile/EditMode/PlayMode validation handoff tied to the task attempt.
A merge-time receipt path that connects task, relevant canon, integrated commit, tests, and human approval.
Scoped GDD/task impact handling and task supersession for moving canon.
Task-specific tests and scene/action integration for the first real gameplay slice.
Throughput telemetry: elapsed time, model time, human minutes, retries, Unity cycles, and failure causes.

deliverables: Human-approved micro-contract resolving NSC-003 input arbitration, cancellation, arrival/pathing, and restriction semantics; supersede the current overconfident single-agent contract rather than dispatching it unchanged.
Use one manually created writable worktree and one coding worker; add no new supervisor, graph, reconciliation, or provider framework.
Implement Input Actions-backed pointer projection plus click-to-destination/held-pointer movement, restriction, suspension, and reset in PlayerMovement, with canonical scene/builder wiring.
Add focused pure/component and Play Mode tests mapped to the micro-contract, then run the existing clean Unity validation path and preserve XML outside the repository during execution.
Perform one human Play Mode movement-feel and input-conflict check.
Merge manually and publish one concise delivery receipt using existing evidence concepts.
Record elapsed time, agent time, human minutes, retries, context size, Unity cycles, and every manual intervention.
next_slice.proof_of_value: From a clean base, complete and merge the playable slice within one working day with no pipeline-framework code, no canonical-asset mutation during tests, passing compile/EditMode/PlayMode evidence, and no more than about 60 minutes of human orchestration. Restart the worker once from a checkpoint to prove recovery. If this cannot be done, the observed blocker—not the roadmap—defines the next infrastructure slice.
next_slice.title: Gameplay-first mouse movement delivery experiment
next_slice.why: It attacks a visible current GDD/repository gap, exercises Input Actions, shared targeting, scene integration, Unity validation, repair, recovery, and truthful completion, and will reveal whether the existing machinery provides leverage or merely overhead.

observed_failure_solutions: Repository-persisted state addresses real cross-session and stale-assignment problems better than conversation memory.
The current GDD RAG rejects the genuinely stale Assignment 4 knowledge base and binds retrieval to current canon.
Runtime feedback re-entering GER solved two camera implementations that passed static review but failed in Unity.
The no-op progress guard solved an observed refiner that claimed implementation without changing Assets.
Bounded retries/circuit breaking addressed the demonstrated possibility of repeated failed camera refinements.
The non-saving builder seam, committed-scene conformance tests, clean Unity runner, and scene centralization address observed test-mutation and duplicate-scene-authority risks.
Removing mutable completion from task contracts and deriving conformance from committed evidence addresses a real unsafe authority design, although it has not yet been connected back to readiness.
Deterministic graph validation usefully catches malformed identity, dependency cycles, and structural corruption, though it does not catch semantic/path drift.
overengineering: Approximately 28,000 lines of current pipeline and reconciliation Python precede the first production gameplay delivery loop.

The one-time graph bootstrap has generator, independent verification, refinement, approval, seeding, migration, and multiple immutable history views; most should not participate in ordinary development.
Thirty-seven detailed contracts and 59 edges over-plan a very small prototype while at least one supposedly single-agent contract still requires substantial human design clarification.
AgentRuntime and TaskExecution create nested immutable audit artifacts but cannot yet edit or validate the game.

Planner, evaluator, validator, fresh diff reviewer, GER evaluator, and human reviewer roles overlap; one worker, deterministic tests, one fresh review, and one human experiential gate are sufficient initially.
A 9,216-word GDD has a dedicated roughly 1,200-line production RAG implementation. The existing retriever is usable, but expanding it into a context/scanner platform is not yet justified.
Provider migration and eight-role ArchitectureReview execution consumed attention without increasing gameplay throughput.
Multiple handoff documents repeat mutable current-state narratives and have already diverged.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary boundaries are: human-approved design/decisions; bounded task intent; integrated main as implementation truth; test/runtime evidence; and explicit human experiential/merge approval.
The GDD should not own volatile repository facts. Canonical scene paths, installed components, and build state belong to Git/project inspection or a generated inventory.
Task contracts should reference relevant canon rather than duplicate long excerpts and bootstrap repository observations as quasi-current state.
Reconciliation snapshots are useful historical audits but duplicate the living task graph when treated as a routine synchronization mechanism.

The task contract, conformance record, test XML, TaskExecution request, AgentRuntime request/result, provider log, and future supervisor journal risk becoming overlapping audit stores. One attempt manifest plus raw evidence is enough.
Conformance checks hash consistency, not semantic correctness: NSC-023 can be reported conformant while current canon still identifies the deleted scene as authoritative.
The evaluator checks current HEAD rather than an explicit integration ref, so it cannot independently prove 'merged to main.'
The schema-v2 correction removed unsafe mutable completion but left readiness entirely disabled; the work graph is durable planning data, not an operational autonomy engine.
START_HERE, CURRENT_STATE, master context, milestone contexts, and ADRs duplicate current state. Durable documentation only helps if one compact status file is canonical and mechanically checked.
strong_decisions: Deterministic tools establish facts; model claims do not.
Keep implementation workers bounded to one approved task.
Start with one worker and isolated branches/worktrees.
Treat Unity/runtime evidence as first-class and retain human game-feel/visual checks.
Use bounded repair loops with no-progress detection and circuit breakers.
Do not let implementation agents silently invent missing design.
Protect canonical assets from test mutation and distinguish builder capability from committed-artifact state.
Keep reconciliation snapshots historical and require review before graph changes.
Derive completion/conformance from committed evidence rather than editable task status.
Defer parallelism and automatic merge until repeated single-ticket delivery succeeds.
structural_flaws: There is no vertical path from task selection through writable execution, Unity validation, recovery, merge, and readiness. The architecture currently stops before development begins.
Moving-target synchronization is not implemented. A scene relocation immediately left canon, task contracts, project requirements, and resource locks stale.
The structural validator accepts nonexistent operational resource paths and semantically obsolete task contracts.
The GDD is both design canon and a repository-state narrative, creating an irresolvable authority collision when implementation changes first.
The entire GDD hash is simultaneously over-conservative for unrelated edits and insufficient to prove semantic applicability.
The current conformance evaluator does not establish integration into main despite documentation using integrated main as authority.
NSC-003 is labeled concrete and single-agent while the repository's own current-state document lists unresolved design and integration questions.
Status documentation is not reliably resumable because the designated entry documents contradict each other at the same commit.
Infrastructure milestone ordering has optimized local correctness of individual subsystems rather than end-to-end player-value throughput.
result.throughput_assessment: Current leverage is low. The system can validate graph structure, retrieve current GDD chunks, invoke read-only providers, and derive one retrospective camera baseline, but it cannot autonomously select, edit, test, merge, or complete gameplay work. Repository history shows large infrastructure throughput but essentially no new gameplay after Assignment 6. If forbidden to build infrastructure for one slice, the first break is immediate: AgentRuntime cannot write or execute approved commands and taskcontrol cannot authorize a task. Bypassing those gates manually, NSC-003 then breaks on unresolved input/pathing semantics and the need for host Unity validation. Assignment 6 suggests bounded agents plus Unity feedback can help, but material speed should not be claimed until at least two consecutive gameplay slices use the same thin delivery lane without new orchestration code.
result.verdict_reason: The project has selected several correct safety principles, but the implemented architecture is not fundamentally sound as an operational autonomous-development system yet. Its authorities already drift, semantic synchronization is missing, conformance does not prove integration, and the graph cannot dispatch. At the same time, substantial speculative machinery has displaced gameplay. Reorganize around a minimal, moving-canon-aware, one-ticket Unity delivery loop and make every further subsystem earn itself through an observed failure.
